definition: Dispatch capacity is the maximum amount of power a plant can produce; break-even cost is the lowest price a plant can accept for its output and still avoid a loss.
core_idea: These two figures are what populate a generation stack for each plant: capacity determines the width of its block, break-even cost determines its vertical position.
key_points: Break-even cost is heavily influenced by fuel costs for fuel-dependent generators (e.g., natural gas)
Capacity is the amount of power (in MWh) a plant can contribute
relationships: Underpins bid placement strategy and the generation stack ordering
trading_implications: Break-even cost acts as an approximate floor for a plant's bid price
